content:
nina: Quick heads-up: billing showed GPU-hours attributed to the wrong customer again when we did multi-tenant batches + regional failovers. We need a robust way to carry attribution through routing, batching, and retries. Thoughts?

ben: Seen it. Current pipeline only tags at the GPU process where we no longer have original ingress context after reroutes.

priya: Three practical approaches I can think of: 1) sticky attribution header at ingress that follows the request, 2) inexpensive ingress event that emits a mapping id to a side datastore and we write the id into the request, or 3) after-the-fact reconstruction from logs (best-effort).

matt: Agree. Header is simplest but increases header/cardinality surface. Mapping id avoids big strings but needs a stable resolver. Reconstruction is brittle.

nina: If we do a header it should be minimal. Example candidate: `X-RDW-TRACECOST: f=H(tenant:12345)|r=chat-v1|c=exp3|b=grp9`

ben: Please H() the tenant. Also normalize route names to low-cardinality buckets (chat-v1 -> chat-1) so we don't explode indices.

priya: Also: store two labels: origin (who requested) and effective (which model actually executed). That lets us charge the requester while still splitting GPU-time across actual model variants.

matt: For retries: append-only semantics or keep origin+effective. If a retry triggers a fallback to a lower-cost model, origin stays same, effective changes. GPU logs should record effective.

nina: On ingestion/query side I don't want long strings in hot indexes. Plan: compute a stable fingerprint at edge (fingerprint -> small id) and include that id in headers. A separate mapping table resolves id -> fields for joins.

ben: That mirrors a lightweight collector pattern. Edge computes fingerprint deterministically (same algo everywhere), writes mapping record async to mapping store. If mapping arrives late, join-on-null = unknown.

priya: Operational safety: fingerprinting algorithm must be deterministic & stable across regions and deploys. Also rate-limit new fingerprints and collapse noisy variants into `unknown-cohort` when threshold exceeded.

matt: Add metrics that count how often we get `unknown-cohort` and mapping-lag. Alerting on both.

ops-bot: rollout: router change to inject X-RDW-FP header into upstream requests deployed to staging at 2024-11-06T09:12:00Z (canary 5%). Build rwd-obs-1142.

nina: Next actions: Priya + Ben to author a short RFC with header/fingerprint format, hashing algorithm, and mapping table contract. Matt to write the semantic rules for origin/effective on retries and fallbacks. I'll draft an ops playbook for unknown-cohort alerts and automated throttles. Target: RFC + prototype by EOW.

priya: I'll start the RFC now and include test cases (mixed-tenant batch, regional failover).

ben: I'll build a tiny mapping resolver and example SQL join that shows GPU logs joined with mapping table to produce billing-ready rows.

matt: I'll add an integration test in harness (org/integration/testcases/attr-fallback) that simulates cross-shard batching and model fallback to validate attribution.

nina: Great. Keep this thread for short notes; we'll review RFC formally. :white_check_mark:
